doc.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

title: Reincarnation and rejecting tribalism
summary: He believes in a continuing spirit and traces his rejection of tribalism to a nun's remark during first communion.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Wow. Yup. Well here’s a — I don’t think I’ve ever asked this question of anybody but I’ll try it out on you. Do you believe in any kind of reincarnation?

Yes. I do. I think that there is a spirit, because I don’t know if we come back as the same type of being, or even on this planet you know. But I do think that when we leave something, some echo of us, maybe it goes to another dimension literally, but you know I have no idea where it goes and I’m not — I have no philosophy about that. But I don’t think it ends.

Okay. Because I’m often curious about, well in your case, why does someone born in Cleveland, right, become attracted to the African influence or Brazilian music or where do these things come from? Why are you opened up to those kinds of opportunities?

You know I can trace that back to one phrase when I was studying for my first holy communion and some witch-like nun said, “You know if you’re not Catholic you’re going to hell.” And I thought, oh my God, all the people preceding Jesus Christ, all the — they’re all in hell? And I rejected it right there. And so any — I reject tribalism of any kind. And I think that countries and religions and races and nationalities, those are all tribes. And if we can leave the tribal then we can ascend as a whole. So that’s why I don’t feel superior or inferior to anyone, but I certainly don’t feel superior to anyone. And if you feel that way then everyone has validity, you know? Everyone. Somebody cleaning the street or the president — well I don’t want to go there.
Well I wanted to go there.
